$~$

The overall purpose of this project is to identify if there are predilections for certain germline p53 mutations in certain tissues due to similar developmental origins, which can then potentially influence specific epigenomic landscapes in these tissues. As germline p53 mutations would be present in all cells from conception, they would be carried through all developmental tissues and their organ derivatives, and thus could shape the unique epigenetics specific to tissues. Consequently, these enrichments of mutations could favor carcinogenesis in specific tissues.

$~$

# **Libraries Used and Functions** {#librariesandfx}

$~$

This code calls all the packages used in this document's analysis, and sets a seed for reproducibility. I also introduce a function to add significance stars to p-values generated by summary tables later on.

$~$


``` r
#load (and install if needed) pacman and use it to load important packages
if (!require("pacman", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("pacman"); library(pacman)
pacman::p_load(BiocManager, stringr, dplyr, tidyverse, ggplot2, kableExtra, knitr, devtools, rmarkdown, readr, readxl, patchwork, data.table, scales, grid, gridExtra, condformat, cowplot, janitor, pivottabler, reshape2, tibble, gtools, ggpubr, ggrepel, RColorBrewer, ComplexHeatmap, bookdown, ggalluvial, gt, gtsummary, webshot2, dendextend, factoextra, NbClust, fpc, cluster, fossil, nnet, MASS, survminer, survival, ggh4x, corrplot, ggstats, car, caret, venn)

#update all loaded packages
#pacman::p_update() 

#set seed for reproducibility
set.seed(1212)

# create function to show significance stars in gt summary tables 
pvalue_with_stars <- function(x) {
  dplyr::case_when(
    x < 0.001 ~ paste0(style_pvalue(x, digits = 3), " (***)"),
    x < 0.01 ~ paste0(style_pvalue(x, digits = 3), " (**)"),
    x < 0.05 ~ paste0(style_pvalue(x, digits = 3), " (*)"),
    TRUE ~ style_pvalue(x, digits = 3)
  )
}

# create function to pivot wider multinomial gt summary tables
multinom_pivot_wider <- function(x) {
  # check inputs match expectatations
  if (!inherits(x, "tbl_regression") || !inherits(x$model_obj, "multinom")) {
    stop("`x=` must be class 'tbl_regression' summary of a `nnet::multinom()` model.")
  }
  
  # create tibble of results
  df <- tibble::tibble(outcome_level = unique(x$table_body$groupname_col))
  df$tbl <- 
    purrr::map(
      df$outcome_level,
      function(lvl) {
        gtsummary::modify_table_body(
          x, 
          ~dplyr::filter(.x, .data$groupname_col %in% lvl) %>%
            dplyr::ungroup() %>%
            dplyr::select(-.data$groupname_col)
        )
      }
    )
  
  tbl_merge(df$tbl, tab_spanner = paste0("**", df$outcome_level, "**"))
}

# create function to put n numbers and other stats above plots
stat_box_data <- function(y) {
  return( 
    data.frame(
      y = 1.35 + 1.1 * max(y), 
      label = paste('n =', length(y), '\n'
                    #,
                    #'mean =', round(mean(y), 2), "\n"
                    ,
                    "median =", round(median(y), 2), "\n"
                    )
    )
  )
}
```

# **Input Data** {#inputdata}

$~$

First I downloaded the entire germline variant dataset from the TP53 Database [@tp53database2022], downloaded from this site: <https://tp53.cancer.gov/view_data?bq_view_name=GermlineDownload>. To get to this page, go to <https://tp53.cancer.gov/> --\> Germline Variants --\> Data Downloads Germline Variants --\> TP53 germline variants and family history (data file) --\> click Preview icon to get to filterable data table --\> download entire table without any filters.

$~$

I also took p53 mutations described in Figure 7J of @chen2021 as being transcriptionally rescued after the administration of arsenic trioxide (ATO) i.e. all mutations with more than 2-fold change of transcriptional activity (upper right and lower right quadrants). ATO has been proposed as a possible therapeutic agent for Li-Fraumeni Syndrome where short doses could prevent cancer incidence [@Pantziarka2022]. So it would be good to track which mutations in the TP53 database germline mutant dataset could potentially be rescued by this agent.

$~$

I also downloaded information for all p53 mutants tested for ATO rescue from <http://www.rescuep53.net/explore.html> and took Supplementary Table S6 from @song2023. The site was created from the results of this paper and Supplementary Table S6 specifically lists which mutations are type 1, 2a (both of which had notable ATO-mediated rescue), 2b, or 3 mutants (either less effectively rescued or not rescued at all after ATO). To get mutations from the website, I went to <http://www.rescuep53.net/explore.html>, changed the upper left dropdown to show all 800 mutations, and manually copied and pasted all the columns' information into an Excel file, which I have then read in below.

$~$

I also took p53 mutations described in Figure 5C of @tang2022 as being transcriptionally rescued after the administration of potassium antimony tartrate (PAT).

$~$

In this code, I have then read in the entire downloaded file as a dataframe, removed any duplicated rows (which were none), and have just displayed the first six rows of the table to get a preview of the data.

$~$

# **Cleaning Input Data** {#cleaningdata}

$~$

Next, I cleaned the data by removing entries with nondescript cancers, clarifying mutations without specific residues, improving mutation formatting, only keeping entries of confirmed germline carriers, removing a mutation documented as a founder effect, collapsing similar category cancers into one cancer type, compiling ages at diagnosis or follow-up into age strata, and removing mutations which have no ages or sexes listed. I am considering the short topology column for cancers because not every cancer has good detailed annotations for specific cancer types. However, for adrenal gland and bone cancers, they are primarily comprised of 1 morphology each, so I am using that morphology for subsequent calculations. I then saved this cleaned data (along with a slight modification to include certain morphologies) as its own CSV file which can be read into R again or used on its own at any time. Moreover, I split the data into patients with either 1 cancer or multiple cancers to do individual analyses, and saved them as separate CSV files.

$~$


``` r
#remove data with unknown site or other sites short topology for cancer
origdbcleaned <- origdbdistinct %>% 
  filter(!Short_topo %in% c("OTHER SITES", 
                            "UNKNOWN SITE")) %>%
  remove_rownames()

#concatenate codon number and mutation type to "p.?" mutations which have unspecified residues and rename intronic/splice mutations as such
origdbcleaned <- origdbcleaned %>% 
  mutate(ProtDescription = ifelse(ProtDescription %in% c("p.?"),
                                  paste(ProtDescription, 
                                        Codon_number, 
                                        Effect,
                                        sep = "-"), 
                                  ProtDescription)) %>%
  mutate(ProtDescription = gsub("\\?-0-splice|\\?-0-intronic",
                                "Intronic",
                                ProtDescription)) %>% 
  remove_rownames()

#remove "p." prefix from all mutations to clean up visually
origdbcleaned$ProtDescription <- substring(origdbcleaned$ProtDescription, 3) 

#only keep data of confirmed germline carriers
origdbcleaned <- origdbcleaned %>% 
  filter(Germline_carrier == "Confirmed") %>%
  remove_rownames()

#remove R337H data - Brazilian founder effect often removed from published papers' analyses
origdbcleaned <- origdbcleaned %>% 
  filter(ProtDescription != "R337H") %>%
  remove_rownames()

#combine BONES (other) and BONES (limbs) short topologies into 1 BONES short topology, and COLON and RECTUM, NOS short topologies into 1 COLORECTUM short topology
origdbcleaned <- origdbcleaned %>%
  mutate(Short_topo = ifelse(Short_topo %in% c('BONES (other)',
                                               'BONES (limbs)'), 
                             'BONES', 
                             Short_topo)) %>%
  mutate(Short_topo = ifelse(Short_topo %in% c("COLON",
                                               "RECTUM",
                                               "COLORECTUM, NOS"),
                             "COLORECTUM",
                             Short_topo))

#duplicate age at diagnosis column so that can add age at follow-up without disturbing original column, rearrange column order for ease in viewing, and wherever no age at diagnosis, add age at follow-up instead if it's present
origdbcleaned$Age_dx_follow <- origdbcleaned$Age_at_diagnosis
origdbcleaned <- origdbcleaned %>% 
  relocate(Age_at_diagnosis, 
           Age_dx_follow,
           .after = Age) %>%
  mutate(Age_dx_follow = ifelse(is.na(origdbcleaned$Age_dx_follow),
                                Age,
                                Age_dx_follow))

#add age stratum column ~ every 10 yrs of pts, to have at least 100 entries per stratum
origdbcleaned <- origdbcleaned %>%
  transform(Age_stratum = ifelse(Age_dx_follow <= 9,
                                 "0-9",
                                 "notyet")) %>%
  transform(Age_stratum = ifelse(Age_dx_follow >= 10 & Age_dx_follow <= 19,
                                 "10-19",
                                 Age_stratum)) %>%
  transform(Age_stratum = ifelse(Age_dx_follow >= 20 & Age_dx_follow <= 29,
                                 "20-29",
                                 Age_stratum)) %>%
  transform(Age_stratum = ifelse(Age_dx_follow >= 30 & Age_dx_follow <= 39,
                                 "30-39",
                                 Age_stratum)) %>%
  transform(Age_stratum = ifelse(Age_dx_follow >= 40,
                                 "40 and up",
                                 Age_stratum)) %>% 
  relocate(Age_stratum,
           .after = Age_dx_follow) %>% 
  drop_na(Age_stratum) %>%
  drop_na(Sex) %>% 
  distinct()

# identify pts with multiple distinct mutations and remove them, so that only have pts with 1 mut each
pts_dup_muts <- origdbcleaned %>% 
  dplyr::select(c(ProtDescription, 
                  Individual_code)) %>% 
  group_by(Individual_code) %>% 
  filter(n() > 1) %>% # first get all pts with multiple entries regardless of muts
  distinct() %>% # only keep pts with multiple entries and multiple distinct muts
  group_by(Individual_code) %>% 
  filter(n() > 1) %>% # get all pts with multiple distinct muts
  arrange(Individual_code) %>%
  pull(Individual_code) %>%
  unique()

origdbcleaned <- origdbcleaned %>%
  subset(!(Individual_code %in% pts_dup_muts)) %>%
  distinct()

# CHECK WHICH ADRENAL CANCERS ARE THERE WHICH ARE HIGHEST IN 0-9YO, ARE THEY ACC? - yes mostly ACC
# CHECK WHICH BRAIN CANCERS ARE THERE WHICH ARE HIGHEST IN 0-9YO - many types, quite a few of choroid plexus carcinoma and medulloblastoma
# CONSULT LITERATURE TO SEE IF THESE ABOVE ADRENAL AND BRAIN CANCER TYPES ARE THE MOST COMMON IN 0-9

# need to specify short topology as more detailed cancers so that results are a little more informative, 
# we already know from literature that the most common LFS tumors are bones, brain, breast, adrenal, soft tissues, 
# after looking through the data, choosing to rename adrenal and bones because most adrenal tumors are ACC and most bone tumors are osteosarcomas, 
# can make piecharts of non adrenal and bones cancers breakdown, 
# so can use express morphologies for adrenal and bones for pivot tables and subsequent calculations
# change short topologies to have express morphologies of adrenal and bones, otherwise retain original short topologies
breakdown <- origdbcleaned %>% 
  transform(Short_topo = ifelse(Short_topo %in% c("ADRENAL GLAND",
                                                  "BONES"),
                                Morphology,
                                Short_topo)) %>% 
  remove_rownames()

# to clean up formatting in short topology and morphology columns, remove NOS (not otherwise specified) and (C#._) characters
breakdown$Short_topo <- gsub(", NOS",
                             "", 
                             breakdown$Short_topo)
breakdown$Short_topo <- gsub("\\(C.*", 
                             "", 
                             breakdown$Short_topo)
breakdown$Morphology <- gsub(", NOS",
                             "", 
                             breakdown$Morphology)
breakdown$Morphology <- gsub("\\(C.*", 
                             "", 
                             breakdown$Morphology)

# combine similarly named morphologies together to collapse down and remove whitespace at beginning and end of words
breakdown <- breakdown %>% 
  transform(Morphology = ifelse(Morphology %in% c("Carcinoma"),
                                "Cancer",
                                Morphology)) %>% 
  transform(Morphology = ifelse(Morphology %in% c("Infiltrating ductular carcinoma "),
                                "Infiltrating duct carcinoma ",
                                Morphology)) %>% 
  mutate_if(is.character, 
            trimws) %>% 
  distinct() %>% 
  remove_rownames()

# num total families in dataset
n_distinct(breakdown$Family_code) # 960

# find patients which have multiple cancers for individual analyses
# remove patients which didn't have cancer at follow-up and with no age of diagnosis
origdbdefcancer <- breakdown %>% 
  subset(Unaffected == "false") %>% 
  drop_na(Age_at_diagnosis) %>% 
  distinct()

# find patients listed once or multiple times, subset data to such patients, and compare if equivalent
ptswithcancer <- origdbdefcancer %>% 
  count(Individual_code, 
        Age_at_diagnosis, 
        Short_topo, 
        Morphology, 
        sort = TRUE) %>% 
  distinct() %>% 
  remove_rownames()
ptswithcancer <- ptswithcancer %>% 
  count(Individual_code,
        sort = TRUE) %>% 
  distinct() %>% 
  remove_rownames()

solepts <- ptswithcancer %>% 
  subset(n == 1) %>% 
  remove_rownames()
solepts <- solepts[order(-solepts$n),] %>% 
  remove_rownames()
origdbsolecancer <- origdbdefcancer %>% 
  subset(origdbdefcancer$Individual_code %in% solepts$Individual_code) %>% 
  distinct()
all(origdbsolecancer$Individual_code %in% solepts$Individual_code) # should be TRUE in console

multpts <- ptswithcancer %>% 
  subset(n > 1) %>% 
  remove_rownames()
multpts <- multpts[order(-multpts$n),] %>% 
  remove_rownames()
origdbmultcancer <- origdbdefcancer %>% 
  subset(origdbdefcancer$Individual_code %in% multpts$Individual_code) %>% 
  distinct()
all(origdbmultcancer$Individual_code %in% multpts$Individual_code) # should be TRUE in console

# add cancer freq status to breakdown which also has no cancer pts
breakdown <- breakdown %>% 
  mutate(cancer_freq_pt_type = dplyr::case_when(Individual_code %in% solepts$Individual_code ~ "sole",
                                                Individual_code %in% multpts$Individual_code ~ "multiple",
                                                Unaffected == "true" ~ "none",
                                                TRUE ~ "notyet"))

# #save cleaned, breakdown, def, multiple, and sole cancer data as CSV
write_csv(origdbcleaned,
          file = paste0(table_path, "origdbcleaned_germline.csv"))
write_csv(breakdown,
          file = paste0(table_path, "breakdown_germline.csv"))
write_csv(origdbdefcancer,
          file = paste0(table_path, "origdbdefcancer_germline.csv"))
write_csv(origdbsolecancer,
          file = paste0(table_path, "origdbsolecancer_germline.csv"))
write_csv(origdbmultcancer,
          file = paste0(table_path, "origdbmultcancer_germline.csv"))

# cleaning up ATO rescue muts files
# vector from cancer cell 2021 paper doesn't need cleaning
cleaned_mut_rescue_ATO_chen_2021 <- orig_mut_rescue_ATO_chen_2021

cleaned_mut_not_rescue_ATO_chen_2021 <- orig_mut_not_rescue_ATO_chen_2021

# don't really need to clean suppl table either since it only has a few cols of interest which are fine as is
cleaned_mut_rescue_ATO_suppl_song_2023 <- orig_mut_rescue_ATO_suppl_song_2023

# remove other characters in mutant col of website data and left-join with classification from suppl table 
cleaned_mut_rescue_ATO_website_song_2023 <- orig_mut_rescue_ATO_website_song_2023 %>%
  transform(MUTANT = gsub(" \\(.*",
                          "",
                          MUTANT)) %>%
  transform(MUTANT = gsub("p.",
                          "",
                          MUTANT)) %>%
  left_join(.,
            cleaned_mut_rescue_ATO_suppl_song_2023 %>%
              dplyr::select(c(protein_change,
                              mut_classification)),
            by = c("MUTANT" = "protein_change")) %>%
  relocate(mut_classification,
           .after = Summary) %>%
  clean_names()

# compile all muts that can be rescued by ATO, which if present in datasets can be annotated on heatmaps
mut_rescued <- c(cleaned_mut_rescue_ATO_chen_2021,
                 cleaned_mut_rescue_ATO_website_song_2023 %>%
                   subset(transcription_activity_rescuable_by_ato == "Rescuable" & mut_classification %in% c("1",
                                                                                                             "2a")) %>% 
                   pull(mutant)
                 # ,
                 # cleaned_mut_rescue_ATO_suppl_song_2023 %>%
                 #   subset(mut_classification %in% c("1",
                 #                                    "2a")) %>%
                 #   pull(protein_change)
) %>%
  trimws() %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  unique()

# put together ATO muts that are definitely non-rescuable, removing any that happen to be in rescued list
# setdiff(x, y) returns the elements of x that are not in y but asymmetric difference, so setdiff(y, x) gives what elements of y are not in x and could be different answer
mut_not_rescued <- setdiff(c(cleaned_mut_not_rescue_ATO_chen_2021,
                             cleaned_mut_rescue_ATO_website_song_2023 %>%
                               subset(mut_classification %in% c("3")) %>% 
                               pull(mutant)),
                           mut_rescued)

# save rescued mut list to use for somatic analyses too
saveRDS(mut_rescued,
        file = paste0(table_path, 
                      "mut_rescued.rds"))

saveRDS(mut_rescue_PAT,
        file = paste0(table_path, 
                      "mut_rescue_PAT.rds"))

saveRDS(mut_not_rescued,
        file = paste0(table_path, 
                      "mut_not_rescued.rds"))

# output rescued mut list as a csv too
write.csv(mut_rescued %>% parse_number() %>% abs() %>% sort(),
          file = paste0(table_path,
                        "mut_rescued.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

write.csv(mut_rescue_PAT %>% parse_number() %>% abs() %>% sort(),
          file = paste0(table_path,
                        "mut_rescue_PAT.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

write.csv(mut_not_rescued %>% parse_number() %>% abs() %>% sort(),
          file = paste0(table_path,
                        "mut_not_rescued.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
```

$~$

After cleaning the data as above, we are left with 2,080 entries from 1,399 individuals from 960 families. Of these 2,080 entries, 1,936 are in patients with cancer (which are 1,255 individuals), while 144 entries are in patients with no cancer at the time of follow-up (which are 144 individuals). Moreover, of these 2,080 entries,

-   523 are in patients with the strict clinical definition of Li-Fraumeni syndrome,

-   366 are in patients with Li-Fraumeni like for the extended clinical definition of Li-Fraumeni,

-   244 are in patients with a family history of cancer which does not fulfill LFS or any of the LFL definitions,

-   170 are in patients with no family history of cancer,

-   78 are in patients with "other" class,

-   434 are in patients classified as TP53_Chompret, and

-   265 are in patients with NA class.

$~$

Furthermore, there are 1,057 entries from 413 individuals with multiple cancers from 374 families. Moreover, of these 1,057 entries,

-   281 are in patients with the strict clinical definition of Li-Fraumeni syndrome,

-   184 are in patients with Li-Fraumeni like for the extended clinical definition of Li-Fraumeni,

-   90 are in patients with a family history of cancer which does not fulfill LFS or any of the LFL definitions,

-   94 are in patients with no family history of cancer,

-   36 are in patients with "other" class,

-   270 are in patients classified as TP53_Chompret, and

-   102 are in patients with NA class.

$~$

On the other hand, there are 878 entries from 842 individuals with only 1 cancer from 661 families. Moreover, of these 878 entries,

-   220 are in patients with the strict clinical definition of Li-Fraumeni syndrome,

-   145 are in patients with Li-Fraumeni like for the extended clinical definition of Li-Fraumeni,

-   127 are in patients with a family history of cancer which does not fulfill LFS or any of the LFL definitions,

-   69 are in patients with no family history of cancer,

-   42 are in patients with "other" class,

-   132 are in patients classified as TP53_Chompret, and

-   143 are in patients with NA class.

$~$

# **Select Cancers with Sufficient Data** {#selectcancers}

$~$

Next, I organized cancers by descending tumor ID count and identified cancers with at 100 (or 50, in multiple or sole cancer datasets) distinct tumor IDs which would be used for subsequent analysis, and saved this list of top cancers to a CSV file and as an SVG. This cutoff of 100 (or 50) was chosen to ensure a large enough sample size to confirm any trends in mutations seen later on as meaningful.

$~$


``` r
#count number of distinct mutated tumor IDs by short topology and sort descending
origdbcancersunique <- origdbdefcancer %>%
  group_by(Short_topo) %>%
  summarise(count = n_distinct(Tumor_ID))
origdbcancersunique <- origdbcancersunique[order(-origdbcancersunique$count),] %>%
  remove_rownames()

origdbmultcancersunique <- origdbmultcancer %>%
  group_by(Short_topo) %>%
  summarise(count = n_distinct(Tumor_ID))
origdbmultcancersunique <- origdbmultcancersunique[order(-origdbmultcancersunique$count),] %>%
  remove_rownames()

origdbsolecancersunique <- origdbsolecancer %>%
  group_by(Short_topo) %>%
  summarise(count = n_distinct(Tumor_ID))
origdbsolecancersunique <- origdbsolecancersunique[order(-origdbsolecancersunique$count),] %>%
  remove_rownames()

#keep only short topologies with at least 100 unique mutated tumor IDs and sort descending; likewise for mult and sole cancers but keep with at least 50
origdbcancersover100 <- origdbcancersunique %>%
  subset(count >= 100)
origdbcancersover100 <- origdbcancersover100[order(-origdbcancersover100$count),] %>%
  remove_rownames()

origdbmultcancersover100 <- origdbmultcancersunique %>%
  subset(count >= 50)
origdbmultcancersover100 <- origdbmultcancersover100[order(-origdbmultcancersover100$count),] %>%
  remove_rownames()

origdbsolecancersover100 <- origdbsolecancersunique %>%
  subset(count >= 50)
origdbsolecancersover100 <- origdbsolecancersover100[order(-origdbsolecancersover100$count),] %>%
  remove_rownames()

# define core LFS cancers
core_LFS_tumors <- origdbcancersover100$Short_topo

#add total row at bottom of short topologies with at least 100 unique mutated tumor IDs
origdbcancersover100withtotal <- origdbcancersover100 %>%
  adorn_totals() %>%
  remove_rownames()

origdbmultcancersover100withtotal <- origdbmultcancersover100 %>%
  adorn_totals() %>%
  remove_rownames()

origdbsolecancersover100withtotal <- origdbsolecancersover100 %>%
  adorn_totals() %>%
  remove_rownames()
# 
# #save 100 unique mutated tumor IDs topologies as SVG and CSV
write_csv(origdbcancersover100withtotal,
          file = paste0(table_path, "origdbcancersover100withtotal_germline.csv"))
write_csv(origdbmultcancersover100withtotal,
          file = paste0(table_path, "origdbmultcancersover100withtotal_germline.csv"))
write_csv(origdbsolecancersover100withtotal,
          file = paste0(table_path, "origdbsolecancersover100withtotal_germline.csv"))
```

In addition to this list of top 5 cancers, there are 144 individuals with no cancer at the time of follow-up who cumulatively have 144 entries of mutations.

$~$

# **Create Cancer Sequence Table of Individuals with Multiple Cancers** {#cancersequence .hidden .unlisted .unnumbered}

$~$

Since there are 413 patients with at least 2 cancers in their lifetime, I created a cancer sequence table for these patients, similar to Table 2 in @Hisada1998. Thus, I identified the distinct cancers (figuratively collapsing down cancers with duplicate tumor IDs or distinct tumor IDs but same age of diagnosis, same short topology, and same morphology) for each Individual throughout their life and compiled them into a dataframe. I will use this table to make a color-coded map of patients and their cancer landscape over time, as well as stacked barcharts of the proportions of cancers at each incidence (e.g. of all first cancers, what proportion is breast vs. soft tissue vs. other tissue).

$~$



$~$



$~$



$~$

$~$

Furthermore, there are 421 entries (421 distinct tumor samples) from 413 individuals with multiple cancers from 374 families. Moreover, of these 421 entries,

-   111 are in patients with the strict clinical definition of Li-Fraumeni syndrome,

-   72 are in patients with Li-Fraumeni like for the extended clinical definition of Li-Fraumeni,

-   38 are in patients with a family history of cancer which does not fulfill LFS or any of the LFL definitions,

-   36 are in patients with no family history of cancer,

-   18 are in patients with "other" class,

-   103 are in patients classified as TP53_Chompret, and

-   43 are in patients with NA class.

$~$

On the other hand, there are 878 entries (878 distinct tumor samples) from 842 individuals with 1 cancer from 661 families. Moreover, of these 878 entries,

-   220 are in patients with the strict clinical definition of Li-Fraumeni syndrome,

-   145 are in patients with Li-Fraumeni like for the extended clinical definition of Li-Fraumeni,

-   127 are in patients with a family history of cancer which does not fulfill LFS or any of the LFL definitions,

-   69 are in patients with no family history of cancer,

-   42 are in patients with "other" class,

-   132 are in patients classified as TP53_Chompret, and

-   143 are in patients with NA class.

$~$

# **Create Pivot Tables of Mutation Types and Codons** {#pivottables}

$~$

Now the data, which only includes cancers with at least 100 distinct tumor IDs and anyone without cancer or with no age or sex listed, can be used for data analysis. I created pivot tables of the number of mutation categories and mutated codons per cancer, age stratum, and sex, converted them to dataframes and saved them as CSV files, and have previewed the tables as output below. For the datasets of multiple and sole cancers, as well as a breakdown of cancer types within short topologies, I have counted the number of distinct tumor samples. However, for the full dataset, which also includes patients without cancer, I have to count the number of mutations instead of distinct tumor samples, as the numbers wouldn't properly reflect patients without cancer.

$~$


``` r
# pivot table of cancers by tumor ID, regardless of whether in sole or multiple, to see how many events overall
origdbcancersuniquepivot <- PivotTable$new()
origdbcancersuniquepivot$addData(origdbdefcancer)
origdbcancersuniquepivot$addRowDataGroups("Short_topo")
origdbcancersuniquepivot$defineCalculation(calculationName = "Count of cancers",
                                     summariseExpression = "n_distinct(Tumor_ID)")
origdbcancersuniquepivot$sortColumnDataGroups(levelNumber = 1,
                                        orderBy = "calculation",
                                        sortOrder = "desc")
origdbcancersuniquepivot$sortRowDataGroups(levelNumber = 1,
                                     orderBy = "calculation",
                                     sortOrder = "desc")
origdbcancersuniquepivot$evaluatePivot() #doing this instead of renderPivot() which takes too long as it shows an actual pivot table, but we need this as a dataframe anyways for calculations later so we don't need to print a pivot table
```

``` r
demog_df <- origdbjustsolecancersover100 %>%
  dplyr::select(c(Individual_code,
                  Cancer_Label,
                  Age_stratum,
                  Sex,
                  Region,
                  Class,
                  Mode_of_inheritance,
                  Dead
                  # ,
                  # Domain,
                  # Residue_function,
                  # Effect,
                  # DNE_LOFclass,
                  # SIFTClass,
                  # TransactivationClass
  )) %>%
  dplyr::rename(Inheritance = Mode_of_inheritance) %>%
  mutate(Inheritance = dplyr::case_when(Inheritance == "M" ~ "Maternal",
                                        Inheritance == "P" ~ "Paternal",
                                        Inheritance == "de novo" ~ "De novo",
                                        Inheritance == "de novo, mosaic" ~ "De novo, mosaic",
                                        Inheritance == "NA" ~ "Not listed",
                                        TRUE ~ Inheritance)) %>%
  mutate(Class = gsub("TP53_",
                      "",
                      Class)) %>%
  mutate(Class = dplyr::case_when(Class == "FH" ~ "Family history of cancer",
                                  Class == "noFH" ~ "No family history of cancer",
                                  Class == "NA" ~ "Not listed",
                                  TRUE ~ Class))  %>%
  mutate(Sex = dplyr::case_when(Sex == "M" ~ "Male",
                                Sex == "F" ~ "Female",
                                TRUE ~ Sex)) %>%
  mutate(Cancer_Label = factor(Cancer_Label,
                               levels = c(sort(unique(core_LFS_tumors)),
                                          "OTHER")
  )) %>%
  dplyr::rename(Case = Class,
                `Age stratum of diagnosis` = Age_stratum) %>%
  distinct() 

t <- tbl_summary(demog_df %>%
                   dplyr::select(-c(Individual_code)),
                 by = Cancer_Label,
                 sort = list(everything() ~ "frequency",
                             `Age stratum of diagnosis` ~ "alphanumeric"),
                 missing_text = "Not indicated") %>% 
  bold_labels() %>%
  add_stat_label() %>%
  as_gt()
t
```

``` r
demog_df <- origdbjustmultcancersover100 %>%
  dplyr::select(c(Individual_code,
                  #Cancer_Label,
                  Age_stratum,
                  Sex,
                  Region,
                  Class,
                  Mode_of_inheritance,
                  Dead
                  # ,
                  # Domain,
                  # Residue_function,
                  # Effect,
                  # DNE_LOFclass,
                  # SIFTClass,
                  # TransactivationClass
  )) %>%
  dplyr::rename(Inheritance = Mode_of_inheritance) %>%
  mutate(Inheritance = dplyr::case_when(Inheritance == "M" ~ "Maternal",
                                        Inheritance == "P" ~ "Paternal",
                                        Inheritance == "de novo" ~ "De novo",
                                        Inheritance == "de novo, mosaic" ~ "De novo, mosaic",
                                        Inheritance == "NA" ~ "Not listed",
                                        Inheritance == "M&P" ~ "Maternal and paternal",
                                        TRUE ~ Inheritance)) %>%
  mutate(Class = gsub("TP53_",
                      "",
                      Class)) %>%
  mutate(Class = dplyr::case_when(Class == "FH" ~ "Family history of cancer",
                                  Class == "noFH" ~ "No family history of cancer",
                                  Class == "NA" ~ "Not listed",
                                  TRUE ~ Class))  %>%
  mutate(Sex = dplyr::case_when(Sex == "M" ~ "Male",
                                Sex == "F" ~ "Female",
                                TRUE ~ Sex)) %>%
  # mutate(Cancer_Label = factor(Cancer_Label,
  #                              levels = c(sort(unique(core_LFS_tumors)),
  #                                         "OTHER")
  # )) %>%
  dplyr::rename(Case = Class,
                `Age stratum of diagnosis` = Age_stratum) %>%
  distinct() 

t <- tbl_summary(demog_df %>%
                   dplyr::select(-c(Individual_code)),
                 by = Sex,
                 sort = list(everything() ~ "frequency",
                             `Age stratum of diagnosis` ~ "alphanumeric"),
                 missing_text = "Not indicated") %>% 
  bold_labels() %>%
  add_stat_label() %>%
  as_gt()
t
```

``` r
demog_df <- breakdown %>%
  subset(Unaffected == "true") %>%
  dplyr::select(c(Individual_code,
                  #Cancer_Label,
                  Age_stratum,
                  Sex,
                  Region,
                  Class,
                  Mode_of_inheritance,
                  Dead
                  # ,
                  # Domain,
                  # Residue_function,
                  # Effect,
                  # DNE_LOFclass,
                  # SIFTClass,
                  # TransactivationClass
  )) %>%
  dplyr::rename(Inheritance = Mode_of_inheritance) %>%
  mutate(Inheritance = dplyr::case_when(Inheritance == "M" ~ "Maternal",
                                        Inheritance == "P" ~ "Paternal",
                                        Inheritance == "de novo" ~ "De novo",
                                        Inheritance == "de novo, mosaic" ~ "De novo, mosaic",
                                        Inheritance == "NA" ~ "Not listed",
                                        Inheritance == "M&P" ~ "Maternal and paternal",
                                        TRUE ~ Inheritance)) %>%
  mutate(Class = gsub("TP53_",
                      "",
                      Class)) %>%
  mutate(Class = dplyr::case_when(Class == "FH" ~ "Family history of cancer",
                                  Class == "noFH" ~ "No family history of cancer",
                                  Class == "NA" ~ "Not listed",
                                  TRUE ~ Class))  %>%
  mutate(Sex = dplyr::case_when(Sex == "M" ~ "Male",
                                Sex == "F" ~ "Female",
                                TRUE ~ Sex)) %>%
  # mutate(Cancer_Label = factor(Cancer_Label,
  #                              levels = c(sort(unique(core_LFS_tumors)),
  #                                         "OTHER")
  # )) %>%
  dplyr::rename(Case = Class,
                `Age stratum of last follow-up` = Age_stratum
                ) %>%
  distinct() 

t <- tbl_summary(demog_df %>%
                   dplyr::select(-c(Individual_code)),
                 by = Sex,
                 sort = list(everything() ~ "frequency",
                             `Age stratum of last follow-up` ~ "alphanumeric"
                             ),
                 missing_text = "Not indicated") %>% 
  bold_labels() %>%
  add_stat_label() %>%
  as_gt()
t
```

# **Calculating Proportions of Mutation Types and Positions** {#calcproportions}

$~$

Now that I have the counts of mutation types or positions per cancer, age, and sex, I calculated the proportions across all cancers, ages, and sexes for each dataset, i.e. the number of mutations divided by the total number of mutations. I also saved these calculated results as CSV files, expressly labeled entries from patients without cancer or with no ages listed as such (so that figures are appropriately labeled), and subsetted the datasets to only include mutated codons with at least a 1% proportion as well as removing mutations with no ages listed (since our analysis is expressly concerned with listed ages and mutations in age brackets). As the saved CSV files do not have this 1% threshold or non-cancer/non-age labeling, they can be edited later on as needed for other types of analysis. I have displayed a preview of the datasets below.

A 1% proportion threshold was chosen to select for mutations present at relatively substantial levels, as including all mutated residues would lead to an illegible heatmap with hundreds of columns of alterations. Subsequent analysis can indeed include all mutated residues if desired, or impose a different percent threshold, simply by changing the code below and the input data for clustered heatmap generation towards the end. Of note, only the specific mutated codon datasets were subsetted at a 1% proportion threshold; the mutation category datasets have not undergone any threshold cutoff.

$~$


``` r

defcancersuniquepivot_calc <- defcancersuniquepivot %>% 
  dplyr::rename(Total = `Count of cancers`) %>% 
  transform(Short_topo = paste0(Short_topo,
                                " (",
                                format(Total, 
                                      big.mark = ",", 
                                      trim = TRUE),
                                " events)")) %>%
  transform(Short_topo = ifelse(Total == 1,
                                gsub("events",
                                     "event",
                                     Short_topo),
                                Short_topo)) %>% 
  mutate(prop = Total/last(Total)) %>% 
  remove_rownames()

multcancerpivottypenobottom <- multcancerpivottype %>% 
  subset(Short_topo != "Total") %>% 
  transform(Short_topo = paste0(Short_topo,
                                " (",
                                Total,
                                " individuals)")) %>%
  transform(Short_topo = ifelse(Total == 1,
                                gsub("individuals",
                                     "individual",
                                     Short_topo),
                                Short_topo)) %>%
  remove_rownames()

colnames(multcancerpivottypenobottom) <- colnames(multcancerpivottype)

multcancerpivotposnobottom <- multcancerpivotpos %>% 
  subset(Short_topo != "Total") %>%

# call non-cancers of interest as OTHER so that barcharts just show top 5 and OTHER, and only keep core tissues and other tissues with developmental genes

  transform(Cancer_Label = Cancer)

  transform(Cancer_temp = gsub(" \\(.*", 
                               "", 
                               Cancer)) %>%
  subset(Cancer_temp %in% c(origdbcancersover100$Short_topo
                            # ,
                            # "LIVER",
                            # "LUNG",
                            # "KIDNEY",
                            # "PANCREAS"
  )) %>%
  dplyr::select(-Cancer_temp) %>%
  remove_rownames()

                                  "OTHER"))

                                  as.character(Cancer),
                                  "OTHER"))

solecancerpivotclass_melted <- solecancerpivotclass_melted %>%
  mutate(Cancer_Label = Cancer) %>%
  mutate(Class = gsub("TP53_",
                      "",
                      Class)) %>%
  mutate(Class = dplyr::case_when(Class == "FH" ~ "Family history of cancer",
                                  Class == "noFH" ~ "No family history of cancer",
                                  Class == "NA" ~ "Not listed",
                                  TRUE ~ Class))
solecancerpivotinheri_melted <- solecancerpivotinheri_melted %>%
  mutate(Cancer_Label = Cancer) %>%
  mutate(Inheritance = dplyr::case_when(Inheritance == "M" ~ "Maternal",
                                        Inheritance == "P" ~ "Paternal",
                                        Inheritance == "de novo" ~ "De novo",
                                        Inheritance == "de novo, mosaic" ~ "De novo, mosaic",
                                        Inheritance == "NA" ~ "Not listed",
                                        TRUE ~ Inheritance))
```

``` r
  subset(Short_topo == "Total") %>%
  remove_rownames() %>% 
  column_to_rownames("Short_topo") %>% 
  t() %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  rownames_to_column("Mutation") %>%

  filter(str_detect(Mutation, "G245|A347") | Mutation == "Total")
```

``` r
# vectors for pie chart of how most muts are chosen anyways for heatmap
prop <- n_distinct(solecancerpivotpos_melted_over0.01 %>% 
                     drop_na(Proportion) %>% 
                     pull(Mutation) %>%
                     as.vector()) / n_distinct(solecancerpivotpos_melted %>% 
                                                 drop_na(Proportion) %>% 
                                                 pull(Mutation) %>%
                                                 as.vector())
vec <- c(prop,
         1 - prop)
raw <- c(n_distinct(solecancerpivotpos_melted_over0.01 %>% 
                      drop_na(Proportion) %>% 
                      pull(Mutation) %>%
                      as.vector()),
         n_distinct(setdiff(unique(solecancerpivotpos_melted %>% 
                                     drop_na(Proportion) %>% 
                                     pull(Mutation) %>%
                                     as.vector()),
                            unique(solecancerpivotpos_melted_over0.01 %>% 
                                     drop_na(Proportion) %>% 
                                     pull(Mutation) %>%
                                     as.vector()))))

# make prevalence waterfall plots (base R barplots + abline at 1%) of all muts in solecancer to justify why 1% chosen for cutting off
barplot(height = sort(as.numeric(solecancerpivotpos_melted$Proportion) %>% na.omit(),
                      decreasing = TRUE),
        xaxs = "i", # remove space between left side of bars and y axis
        ylab = "Proportion of distinct individuals with cancer", 
        xlab = "p53 mutation",
        main = "Prevalence of p53 Mutations in Distinct Individuals with Cancer",
        font.lab = 2,
        ylim = c(0, plyr::round_any(max(solecancerpivotpos_melted$Proportion,
                                        na.rm = TRUE),
                                    0.1,
                                    f = ceiling)),
        col = ifelse((solecancerpivotpos_melted %>% 
                        #drop_na(Proportion) %>% 
                        pull(Mutation) %>%
                        as.vector()) %in% (solecancerpivotpos_melted_over0.01 %>% 
                                             #drop_na(Proportion) %>% 
                                             pull(Mutation) %>%
                                             as.vector()),
                     "black",
                     "grey"),
        las = 1,
        space = 0,
        border = NA)
abline(h = 0.01,
       col = "red",
       lty = 2,
       lwd = 2)
legend("right",
       legend = c("Subset", 
                  "Other"),
       col = c("black", 
               "gray"),
       bty = "n", # no border around legend
       pch = 15, # filled square shape
       pt.cex = 1.75) # increase shape size in legend
```

``` r
# just get total pts per mut out of all sole
bar_df <- solecancerpivotpos %>% 
  subset(Short_topo == "Total") %>% 
  remove_rownames() %>% 
  column_to_rownames("Short_topo") %>% 
  t() %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  rownames_to_column("Mutation") %>% 
  mutate(Prop = Total/last(Total)) %>% 
  mutate(Proportion = plyr::round_any(Prop * 100,
                                      0.01)) %>% 
  subset(Mutation != "Total")

prop <- n_distinct(solecancerpivotpos_melted_over0.01 %>% 
                     drop_na(Proportion) %>% 
                     pull(Mutation) %>%
                     as.vector()) / n_distinct(origdbjustsolecancersover100$ProtDescription)
vec <- c(prop,
         1 - prop)
raw <- c(n_distinct(solecancerpivotpos_melted_over0.01 %>% 
                      drop_na(Proportion) %>% 
                      pull(Mutation) %>%
                      as.vector()),
         n_distinct(setdiff(unique(origdbjustsolecancersover100$ProtDescription),
                            unique(solecancerpivotpos_melted_over0.01 %>% 
                                     drop_na(Proportion) %>% 
                                     pull(Mutation) %>%
                                     as.vector()))))

barplot(height = sort(as.numeric(bar_df$Prop),
                      decreasing = TRUE),
        xaxs = "i", # remove space between left side of bars and y axis
        ylab = "Proportion of distinct individuals with cancer", 
        xlab = "p53 mutation",
        main = "Prevalence of p53 Mutations in Distinct Individuals with Cancer",
        ylim = c(0, plyr::round_any(max(bar_df$Prop, 
                                        na.rm = TRUE), 
                                    0.01, 
                                    f = ceiling)),
        font.lab = 2,
        col = ifelse(bar_df$Mutation %in% (solecancerpivotpos_melted_over0.01 %>% 
                                             drop_na(Proportion) %>% 
                                             pull(Mutation) %>%
                                             as.vector()),
                     "black",
                     "grey"),
        las = 1,
        space = 0,
        border = NA)
legend("right",
       legend = c("Subset", 
                  "Other"),
       col = c("black", 
               "gray"),
       bty = "n", # no border around legend
       pch = 15, # filled square shape
       pt.cex = 1.75) # increase shape size in legend
```

``` r
# divide down to calc prop of muts in all sole pts, add as new col and mult by 100, remove codon 0 which is intronic muts throughout p53, remove total row, and sort by increasing codon
codon_barplot_df <- solepivotcodon %>%
  mutate(Prop = `Count of distinct patients`/last(`Count of distinct patients`)) %>%
  dplyr::rename(Count_of_distinct_patients = `Count of distinct patients`) %>%
  mutate(Prop_Label = plyr::round_any(Prop * 100,
                                      0.1)) %>%
  subset(!(Codon_number %in% c("0",
                               "Total"))) %>%
  mutate_at("Codon_number",
            as.numeric) %>%
  arrange(Codon_number)

# because not all codons mutated need to add in missing codons as 0 pts and 0 prop
missing_codons <- data.frame(Codon_number = setdiff(1:393, # since p53 has 393 codons
                                                    codon_barplot_df$Codon_number),
                             Count_of_distinct_patients = 0,
                             Prop = 0,
                             Prop_Label = 0)

# add missing codons to df
codon_barplot_df <- full_join(codon_barplot_df,
                              missing_codons) %>%
  arrange(Codon_number)

# barplot, adding codon numbers at intervals and label numbers of codons >= 1.5%
barplot(height = codon_barplot_df$Prop,
        xaxs = "i", # remove space between left side of bars and y axis
        ylab = "Proportion of distinct individuals with cancer", 
        xlab = "Codon",
        main = "Prevalence of p53 Mutations in Distinct Individuals with Cancer",
        #axis.lty = 1,
        #names.arg = codon_barplot_df$Codon_number,
        ylim = c(0, plyr::round_any(max(codon_barplot_df$Prop, 
                                        na.rm = TRUE), 
                                    0.1, 
                                    f = ceiling)),
        font.lab = 2,
        col = dplyr::case_when(codon_barplot_df$Prop >= 0.02 & codon_barplot_df$Codon_number %in% c(175,
                                                                                                    213, 
                                                                                                    245, 
                                                                                                    248, 
                                                                                                    273, 
                                                                                                    282) ~ "purple", 
                               codon_barplot_df$Prop >= 0.02 ~ "red",
                               TRUE ~ "gray"),
        las = 1,
        space = 0,
        border = NA)
axis(side = 1,
     at = c(1, 
            seq(50,
                350, 
                50),
            393))
text(codon_barplot_df$Codon_number[codon_barplot_df$Prop >= 0.015], # x location 
     codon_barplot_df$Prop[codon_barplot_df$Prop >= 0.015], # y location
     codon_barplot_df$Codon_number[codon_barplot_df$Prop >= 0.015], # label to put
     cex = 1, # standard font size
     pos = 3) # text above (x,y) coordinates where it's placed
text(80,
     plyr::round_any(max(codon_barplot_df$Prop, 
                         na.rm = TRUE), 
                     0.1, 
                     f = ceiling) * 0.95,
     paste0("Germline (",
            format(last(solepivotcodon$`Count of distinct patients`), 
                   big.mark = ",", 
                   trim = TRUE),
            " individuals)"),
     cex = 1.5) # increase font size
legend("topright",
       legend = c("≥ 2%",
                  "≥ 2% in somatic too",
                  "Other"),
       col = c("red", 
               "purple", 
               "gray"),
       bty = "n", # no border around legend
       pch = 15, # filled square shape
       pt.cex = 1.75) # increase shape size in legend
```

Furthermore, with this 1% proportion cutoff, there are 103 distinct alterations across the 4 cancers in patients with 2 or more cancers. This cutoff marks a substantial reduction in datapoints to facilitate clustered heatmap generation, as the full dataset before the 1% proportion cutoff has 173 distinct alterations across the 4 cancers.

$~$

On the other hand, with this 1% proportion cutoff, there are 98 distinct alterations across the 5 cancers in patients with 1 cancer. This cutoff marks a substantial reduction in datapoints to facilitate clustered heatmap generation, as the full dataset before the 1% proportion cutoff has 260 distinct alterations across the 5 cancers.

$~$



$~$

$~$

When age is considered, after the 1% proportion cutoff, there are 141 distinct alterations in patients with 2 or more cancers across the 5 age strata. This cutoff again marks a substantial reduction in datapoints to facilitate clustered heatmap generation, as the full dataset before the 1% proportion cutoff has 173 distinct alterations across the 5 age strata.

$~$

When age is considered, after the 1% proportion cutoff, there are 59 distinct alterations in patients with 1 cancer across the 5 age strata. This cutoff again marks a substantial reduction in datapoints to facilitate clustered heatmap generation, as the full dataset before the 1% proportion cutoff has 260 distinct alterations across the 5 age strata.

$~$



$~$

$~$

When sex is considered, after the 1% proportion cutoff, there are 32 distinct alterations in patients with 2 or more cancers. This cutoff again marks a substantial reduction in datapoints to facilitate clustered heatmap generation, as the full dataset before the 1% proportion cutoff has 173 distinct alterations.

$~$

When sex is considered, after the 1% proportion cutoff, there are 31 distinct alterations in patients with 1 cancer. This cutoff again marks a substantial reduction in datapoints to facilitate clustered heatmap generation, as the full dataset before the 1% proportion cutoff has 260 distinct alterations.

$~$

# **Creating Annotations for Heatmaps** {#annotations}

$~$

Next, I have to prepare annotations for the clustered heatmaps I plan to create for these proportions. Here I am preparing to have mutated codons ordered numerically and by p53 domain. Although the domains were partially annotated in the original dataset, for consistency and complete information I have defined the p53 domains as per a few previously published papers [@joruiz2020; @cho1994]. Moreover, I am assigning germ layers to cancers to make it an annotation as well. I also formatted the annotations object to have cancers/no cancer and mutated positions as rownames as this setup is required for the ComplexHeatmap package I will be using.

$~$

``` r
multcancermutinfo <- multcancermutinfo %>% 
  transform(Domain = ifelse(Codon_number >= 1 & Codon_number <= 39, 
                            "TAD1", 
                            "notyet")) %>% 
  transform(Domain = ifelse(Codon_number >= 40 & Codon_number <= 61, 
                            "TAD2", 
                            Domain)) %>% 
  transform(Domain = ifelse(Codon_number >= 62 & Codon_number <= 93, 
                            "PRD", 
                            Domain)) %>% 
  transform(Domain = ifelse(Codon_number >= 94 & Codon_number <= 289, 
                            "DBD", 
                            Domain)) %>% 
  transform(Domain = ifelse(Codon_number >= 112 & Codon_number <= 124, 
                            "DBD L1 loop", 
                            Domain)) %>% 
  transform(Domain = ifelse(Codon_number >= 163 & Codon_number <= 195, 
                            "DBD L2 loop", 
                            Domain)) %>% 
  transform(Domain = ifelse(Codon_number >= 236 & Codon_number <= 251, 
                            "DBD L3 loop", 
                            Domain)) %>% 
  transform(Domain = ifelse(Codon_number >= 290 & Codon_number <= 324, 
                            "HD", 
                            Domain)) %>% 
  transform(Domain = ifelse(Codon_number >= 325 & Codon_number <= 356, 
                            "OD", 
                            Domain)) %>% 
  transform(Domain = ifelse(Codon_number >= 357, 
                            "CTD", 
                            Domain)) %>% 
  transform(Domain = ifelse(Codon_number < 1, 
                            "NA", 
                            Domain)) %>%
  transform(Rescuable = ifelse(ProtDescription %in% mut_rescued,
                             "Rescuable by ATO",
                             "Not documented"))

  transform(Cancer_temp = gsub(" \\(.*",

  transform(Germ_Layer = ifelse(Cancer_temp %in% c("LUNG",

                                                   "PANCREAS"),

  #                              "Other tumor")) %>%
  dplyr::select(-Cancer_temp)

#sort dataframe of cancer by alphabetical germ layer and then by alphabetical cancer
# origdbcancersinfo <- origdbcancersinfo[with(origdbcancersinfo, 
#                                             order(Germ_Layer, 
#                                                   Cancer)), ] %>% 
#   remove_rownames()

multcancersinfo <- multcancersinfo[with(multcancersinfo, 
                                        order(Germ_Layer, 
                                              Cancer)), ] %>% 
  remove_rownames()

solecancersinfo <- solecancersinfo[with(solecancersinfo, 
                                        order(Germ_Layer, 
                                              Cancer)), ] %>% 
  remove_rownames()

#need rownames to be things to match for annotation in complexheatmap, so add cancers to rownames
# rownames(origdbcancersinfo) <- origdbcancersinfo$Cancer
rownames(multcancersinfo) <- multcancersinfo$Cancer
rownames(solecancersinfo) <- solecancersinfo$Cancer
```

# **Formatting Data for Cancer Sequence Figures** {#cancerseqplotprod .hidden .unlisted .unnumbered}

$~$


``` r
# preparing for stacked barchart of distribution of cancers in each incidence of cancer
#make table of how many times a cancer was present as first, second, third, etc. cancer
cancerspertime <- cancersperpt %>% 
  count(Short_topo, 
        cancer_incidence)
cancerspertime <- cancerspertime[order(-cancerspertime$n),] 
cancerspertime <- cancerspertime[gtools::mixedorder(cancerspertime$cancer_incidence),] %>% 
  remove_rownames()
cancerspertime_pivot <- pivot_wider(cancerspertime,
                                    names_from = cancer_incidence,
                                    values_from = n) %>% 
  adorn_totals(where = c("col")) 
cancerspertime_pivot <- cancerspertime_pivot[order(-cancerspertime_pivot$Total),] %>% 
  adorn_totals(where = c("row")) %>%  
  remove_rownames()

#selecting cancers in at least 50 patients and assigning germ layers (although cannot color by germ layers if not all cancers are assigned germ layers, just pre-emptive labeling)
geomtilecancers <- cancerspertime_pivot %>% 
  head(5) %>% # get top 5 cancers to also capture ACC
  #subset(Short_topo != "Total" & Total >= 50) %>% 
  dplyr::select(Short_topo) %>% 
  distinct() %>% 
  transform(Germ_Layer = ifelse(Short_topo %in% c("SOFT TISSUES", "Osteosarcoma", "Adrenal cortical carcinoma"), 
                                "Mesoderm", 
                                "notyet")) %>% 
  transform(Germ_Layer = ifelse(Short_topo %in% c("BREAST", "BRAIN"), 
                                "Ectoderm", 
                                Germ_Layer)) %>% 
  remove_rownames()

# do cancers divided by time (first 3 cancers have adequate pt number), so divide vertically instead of horizontally
# remove total column and only keep columns with at least 100 pts
cancerspertime_nototalcol <- cancerspertime_pivot %>% 
  dplyr::select(!Total) %>% 
  select_if(~ any(. >= 100)) %>% 
  remove_rownames()

# divide cancers by time i.e. vertically, but have to create temp df for division because numbers, and then join cancers
tempcol <- cancerspertime_nototalcol[,2:ncol(cancerspertime_nototalcol)]
tempcol <- tempcol/c(tempcol[nrow(tempcol),])
cancerspertime_nototalcol_calc_nobottom <- cancerspertime_nototalcol %>% 
  dplyr::select(Short_topo) %>% 
  cbind(tempcol) %>% 
  subset(Short_topo != "Total") %>% 
  remove_rownames()

# melt for stacked barchart
cancerspertime_melted <- reshape2::melt(cancerspertime_nototalcol_calc_nobottom) %>% 
  dplyr::rename(Tissue = Short_topo,
                Sequence = variable,
                Proportion = value)
cancerspertime_melted$Tissue_modif <- cancerspertime_melted$Tissue 
cancerspertime_melted <- cancerspertime_melted %>% 
  transform(Tissue_modif = ifelse(!(Tissue_modif %in% geomtilecancers$Short_topo),
                                  "OTHER",
                                  Tissue_modif))

# make color-coded version of cancers per pt pivot table via ggplot2 and geom_tile
cancersperpt$cancer_incidence <- factor(cancersperpt$cancer_incidence,
                                        levels = rev(unique(cancersperpt$cancer_incidence)))
cancersperpt$Individual_code <- factor(cancersperpt$Individual_code,
                                       levels = unique(cancersperpt_pivot$Individual_code))

# for less frequent cancers, calling them other and not assigning germ layer
cancersperpt$Short_topo_modif <- cancersperpt$Short_topo
cancersperpt <- cancersperpt %>% 
  transform(Short_topo_modif = ifelse(!(Short_topo_modif %in% geomtilecancers$Short_topo),
                                      "OTHER",
                                      Short_topo_modif)) %>% 
  remove_rownames()
cancersperpt <- full_join(cancersperpt, 
                          geomtilecancers, 
                          by = "Short_topo") %>% 
  transform(Germ_Layer = ifelse(is.na(Germ_Layer),
                                "Not set",
                                Germ_Layer)) %>% 
  remove_rownames()

#assigning colors to tissues and germ layers to potentially use to color the map
# annotationcolorgeomtile <- list(Tissue = RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(n = 6, name = "Paired"),
#                                 Germ_Layer = RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(n = 3, name = "Dark2"))
annotationcolornamedgeomtile <- list(
  Tissue = c(`Adrenal cortical carcinoma` = "#CC79A7",
             BRAIN = "#E69F00", 
             BREAST = "#009E73", 
             Osteosarcoma = "#56B4E9", 
             `SOFT TISSUES` = "#999999",
             OTHER = "#000000"),
  Germ_Layer = c(Ectoderm = "#7570B3",
                 Mesoderm = "limegreen",
                 `Not set` = "lightgray"))
```

As an initial foray into statistical significance, I'm creating contingency tables for chi square tests on various relationships. These contingency tables are using patients from the full datasets before they are subsetted for the top cancers, to include all patients accurately.

# **Analyses of All Individuals with Adrenal Cortical Carcinoma** {#allACCpts}

$~$

$~$


``` r
# subset dataset of all sole and first mult to just ACC
origdb_allACC_mult_pts <- origdbjustmultcancersover100 %>% 
  subset(Short_topo == "Adrenal cortical carcinoma") %>% 
  distinct() %>% 
  remove_rownames()

origdb_allACC_sole_pts <- origdbjustsolecancersover100 %>% 
  subset(Short_topo == "Adrenal cortical carcinoma") %>% 
  distinct() %>% 
  remove_rownames()

# create pivot of number of female and male pts with ACC in each age stratum of diagnosis, replace any NA with 0, add total number of pts in each age stratum to new column pasted with ages, and make anything with 1 individual singular indication of patients
ACC_mult_agestrata_sex <- PivotTable$new()
ACC_mult_agestrata_sex$addData(origdb_allACC_mult_pts)
ACC_mult_agestrata_sex$addRowDataGroups("Age_stratum")
ACC_mult_agestrata_sex$addColumnDataGroups("Sex") 
ACC_mult_agestrata_sex$defineCalculation(calculationName = "Count of distinct patients", 
                                         summariseExpression = "n_distinct(Individual_code)")
ACC_mult_agestrata_sex$sortColumnDataGroups(levelNumber = 1, 
                                            orderBy = "calculation", 
                                            sortOrder = "desc")
ACC_mult_agestrata_sex$sortRowDataGroups(levelNumber = 1, 
                                         orderBy = "calculation", 
                                         sortOrder = "desc")
ACC_mult_agestrata_sex$evaluatePivot() #doing this instead of renderPivot() which takes too long as it shows an actual pivot table, but we need this as a dataframe anyways for calculations later so we don't need to print a pivot table
ACC_mult_agestrata_sex_pivot <- ACC_mult_agestrata_sex$asDataFrame(rowGroupsAsColumns = TRUE) %>% 
  mutate(across(everything(),
                ~ replace_na(.,
                             0))) %>%
  transform(Age = paste0(Age_stratum,
                         " (", 
                         Total,
                         " individuals)")) %>% 
  transform(Age = ifelse(Total == 1,
                         gsub("individuals", 
                              "individual",
                              Age),
                         Age)) %>% 
  remove_rownames()

# divide number of female and male pts by total number of pts per age stratum
ACC_mult_agestrata_sex_pivot_calc <- ACC_mult_agestrata_sex_pivot %>% 
  mutate_at(vars(2:Total), 
            .funs = ~./Total) %>% 
  dplyr::rename(Female = `F`,
                Male = M) 

ACC_sole_agestrata_sex_pivot_calc <- ACC_sole_agestrata_sex_pivot %>% 
  mutate_at(vars(2:Total), 
            .funs = ~./Total) %>% 
  dplyr::rename(Female = `F`,
                Male = M) 

# divide number of mut type pts by total number of pts per age stratum
ACC_mult_agestrata_type_pivot_calc <- ACC_mult_agestrata_type_pivot %>% 
  mutate_at(vars(2:Total), 
            .funs = ~./Total)

ACC_sole_agestrata_type_pivot_calc <- ACC_sole_agestrata_type_pivot %>% 
  mutate_at(vars(2:Total), 
            .funs = ~./Total)

# divide vertically down sex columns to calc proportions of each mut type in each sex, add number of total female and male pts to colnames
ACC_mult_sex_type_pivot_calc <- ACC_mult_sex_type_pivot %>% 
  dplyr::select(-Total) %>% 
  transform(Female = `F`/as.numeric(ACC_mult_sex_type_pivot[nrow(ACC_mult_sex_type_pivot), "F"])) %>% 
  transform(Male = `M`/as.numeric(ACC_mult_sex_type_pivot[nrow(ACC_mult_sex_type_pivot), "M"])) 

names(ACC_mult_sex_type_pivot_calc) <- ifelse(names(ACC_mult_sex_type_pivot_calc) %in% c("Female"),
                                              paste0("Female (",
                                                     as.numeric(ACC_mult_sex_type_pivot[nrow(ACC_mult_sex_type_pivot),
                                                                                        "F"]),
                                                     " individuals)"),
                                              names(ACC_mult_sex_type_pivot_calc))

names(ACC_mult_sex_type_pivot_calc) <- ifelse(names(ACC_mult_sex_type_pivot_calc) %in% c("Male"),
                                              paste0("Male (",
                                                     as.numeric(ACC_mult_sex_type_pivot[nrow(ACC_mult_sex_type_pivot),
                                                                                        "M"]),
                                                     " individuals)"),
                                              names(ACC_mult_sex_type_pivot_calc))

ACC_sole_sex_type_pivot_calc <- ACC_sole_sex_type_pivot %>% 
  dplyr::select(-Total) %>% 
  transform(Female = `F`/as.numeric(ACC_sole_sex_type_pivot[nrow(ACC_sole_sex_type_pivot), "F"])) %>% 
  transform(Male = `M`/as.numeric(ACC_sole_sex_type_pivot[nrow(ACC_sole_sex_type_pivot), "M"])) 

names(ACC_sole_sex_type_pivot_calc) <- ifelse(names(ACC_sole_sex_type_pivot_calc) %in% c("Female"),

names(ACC_sole_sex_type_pivot_calc) <- ifelse(names(ACC_sole_sex_type_pivot_calc) %in% c("Male"),
                                              paste0("Male (",
                                                     as.numeric(ACC_sole_sex_type_pivot[nrow(ACC_sole_sex_type_pivot),
                                                                                        "M"]),
                                                     " individuals)"),
                                              names(ACC_sole_sex_type_pivot_calc))

# remove total row and column and age column which doesn't have indication of number of total patients, melt pivot for ggplot and rename columns to be more sensible
ACC_mult_agestrata_sex_pivot_melted <- ACC_mult_agestrata_sex_pivot_calc %>% 
  dplyr::select(-Total) %>% 
  subset(Age_stratum != "Total") %>% 
  dplyr::select(-Age_stratum) %>% 
  reshape2::melt() %>% 
  dplyr::rename(Sex = variable,
                Proportion = value)

ACC_sole_agestrata_sex_pivot_melted <- ACC_sole_agestrata_sex_pivot_calc %>% 
  dplyr::select(-Total) %>% 
  subset(Age_stratum != "Total") %>% 
  dplyr::select(-Age_stratum) %>% 
  reshape2::melt() %>% 
  dplyr::rename(Sex = variable,
                Proportion = value)

# remove total row and column and age column which doesn't have indication of number of total patients, melt pivot for ggplot and rename columns to be more sensible, make category column as factor with decreasing proportions and other at end
ACC_mult_agestrata_type_pivot_melted <- ACC_mult_agestrata_type_pivot_calc %>% 
  dplyr::select(-Total) %>% 
  subset(Age_stratum != "Total") %>% 
  dplyr::select(-Age_stratum) %>% 
  reshape2::melt() %>% 
  dplyr::rename(Effect = variable,
                Proportion = value)

ACC_mult_agestrata_type_pivot_melted$Effect <- factor(ACC_mult_agestrata_type_pivot_melted$Effect,
                                                      levels = c(levels(ACC_mult_agestrata_type_pivot_melted$Effect)[!(levels(ACC_mult_agestrata_type_pivot_melted$Effect) == "other")],
                                                                 "other"))

ACC_sole_agestrata_type_pivot_melted <- ACC_sole_agestrata_type_pivot_calc %>% 
  dplyr::select(-Total) %>% 
  subset(Age_stratum != "Total") %>% 
  dplyr::select(-Age_stratum) %>% 
  reshape2::melt() %>% 
  dplyr::rename(Effect = variable,
                Proportion = value)

ACC_sole_agestrata_type_pivot_melted$Effect <- gsub("\\.",
                                                    " ",
                                                    ACC_sole_agestrata_type_pivot_melted$Effect)

ACC_sole_agestrata_type_pivot_melted$Effect <- factor(ACC_sole_agestrata_type_pivot_melted$Effect,
                                                      levels = c(unique(ACC_sole_agestrata_type_pivot_melted$Effect)[!(unique(ACC_sole_agestrata_type_pivot_melted$Effect) == "other")],
                                                                 "other"))

# remove total row and sex columns which don't have number of total patients, melt pivot for ggplot and rename columns to be more sensible, make category column as factor with decreasing proportions and other at end
ACC_mult_sex_type_pivot_melted <- ACC_mult_sex_type_pivot_calc %>% 
  subset(Effect != "Total") %>% 
  dplyr::select(-c(`F`,
                   M)) %>% 
  reshape2::melt() %>% 
  dplyr::rename(Sex = variable,
                Proportion = value) %>% 
  arrange(-Proportion)

ACC_mult_sex_type_pivot_melted$Effect <- factor(ACC_mult_sex_type_pivot_melted$Effect,
                                                levels = c(unique(ACC_mult_sex_type_pivot_melted$Effect)[!(unique(ACC_mult_sex_type_pivot_melted$Effect) == "other")],
                                                           "other"))

ACC_sole_sex_type_pivot_melted <- ACC_sole_sex_type_pivot_calc %>% 
  subset(Effect != "Total") %>% 
  dplyr::select(-c(`F`,
                   M)) %>% 
  reshape2::melt() %>% 
  dplyr::rename(Sex = variable,
                Proportion = value) %>% 
  arrange(-Proportion)

ACC_sole_sex_type_pivot_melted$Effect <- factor(ACC_sole_sex_type_pivot_melted$Effect,
                                                levels = c(unique(ACC_sole_sex_type_pivot_melted$Effect)[!(unique(ACC_sole_sex_type_pivot_melted$Effect) == "other")],
                                                           "other"))

# create pivot of mutated residues vs sex in all ACC patients, replace NA with 0, arrange by increasing codon number, add row and column totals
ACC_mult_sex_pos <- PivotTable$new()
ACC_mult_sex_pos$addData(origdb_allACC_mult_pts)
ACC_mult_sex_pos$addRowDataGroups("ProtDescription")
ACC_mult_sex_pos$addColumnDataGroups("Sex") 
ACC_mult_sex_pos$defineCalculation(calculationName = "Count of distinct patients", 
                                   summariseExpression = "n_distinct(Individual_code)")
ACC_mult_sex_pos$sortColumnDataGroups(levelNumber = 1, 
                                      orderBy = "calculation", 
                                      sortOrder = "desc")
ACC_mult_sex_pos$sortRowDataGroups(levelNumber = 1, 
                                   orderBy = "calculation", 
                                   sortOrder = "desc")
ACC_mult_sex_pos$evaluatePivot() #doing this instead of renderPivot() which takes too long as it shows an actual pivot table, but we need this as a dataframe anyways for calculations later so we don't need to print a pivot table
ACC_mult_sex_pos_pivot <- ACC_mult_sex_pos$asDataFrame(rowGroupsAsColumns = TRUE) %>% 
  mutate(across(everything(),
                ~ replace_na(.,
                             0))) %>% 
  arrange(abs(parse_number(ProtDescription))) %>% # arrange muts by increasing codon number
  dplyr::rename(Num_Individuals = Total,
                Mutation = ProtDescription,
                Female = `F`,
                Male = M) %>%
  remove_rownames()

ACC_sole_sex_pos <- PivotTable$new()
ACC_sole_sex_pos$addData(origdb_allACC_sole_pts)
ACC_sole_sex_pos$addRowDataGroups("ProtDescription")
ACC_sole_sex_pos$addColumnDataGroups("Sex") 
ACC_sole_sex_pos$defineCalculation(calculationName = "Count of distinct patients",

ACC_sole_sex_pos$sortRowDataGroups(levelNumber = 1,

ACC_sole_sex_pos_pivot <- ACC_sole_sex_pos$asDataFrame(rowGroupsAsColumns = TRUE) %>%

                ~ replace_na(.,
                             0))) %>% 
  arrange(abs(parse_number(ProtDescription))) %>% # arrange muts by increasing codon number

                Mutation = ProtDescription,
                Female = `F`,
                Male = M) %>%

# pull out damage info from stock ACC data
origdb_allACC_mult_pts_damageinfo <- origdb_allACC_mult_pts %>% 
  dplyr::select(c(ProtDescription, # first few cols are mut info, then agvgdc onwards are damage info
                  AGVGDClass,
                  BayesDel,
                  REVEL,
                  SIFTClass,
                  Polyphen2,
                  TransactivationClass,
                  DNE_LOFclass,
                  DNEclass)) %>% 
  arrange(abs(parse_number(ProtDescription))) %>% 
  distinct() %>% 
  remove_rownames()

origdb_allACC_sole_pts_damageinfo <- origdb_allACC_sole_pts %>% 
  dplyr::select(c(ProtDescription, # first few cols are mut info, then agvgdc onwards are damage info
                  AGVGDClass,
                  BayesDel,
                  REVEL,
                  SIFTClass,
                  Polyphen2,
                  TransactivationClass,
                  DNE_LOFclass,
                  DNEclass)) %>% 
  arrange(abs(parse_number(ProtDescription))) %>% 
  distinct() %>% 
  remove_rownames()

# add damage info to pivot of mut residues in sexes and replace NAs with blanks so that can plot as grid
ACC_mult_sex_pos_pivot_damage <- left_join(ACC_mult_sex_pos_pivot,
                                           origdb_allACC_mult_pts_damageinfo,
                                           by = c("Mutation" = "ProtDescription")) %>% 
  mutate(across(2:ncol(.),
                ~ str_replace(.,
                              "NA",
                              ""))) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.character),
                ~ replace_na(.,
                             "")))

ACC_sole_sex_pos_pivot_damage <- left_join(ACC_sole_sex_pos_pivot,
                                           origdb_allACC_sole_pts_damageinfo,
                                           by = c("Mutation" = "ProtDescription")) %>% 
  mutate(across(2:ncol(.),
                ~ str_replace(.,
                              "NA",
                              ""))) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.character),
                ~ replace_na(.,
                             "")))

# add damage info to pivot of mut residues in age strata, replace NAs with blanks so that can plot as grid
ACC_mult_agestrata_pos_pivot_damage <- left_join(ACC_mult_agestrata_pos_pivot,

  mutate(across(where(is.character),
                ~ replace_na(.,
                             "")))

ACC_sole_agestrata_pos_pivot_damage <- left_join(ACC_sole_agestrata_pos_pivot,

# divide vertically down age pos and sex pos columns and subset to just residues shown in heatmaps i.e. >= 1%, rename cols for agestrata calc dfs because R changes them per naming conventions
ACC_mult_sex_pos_pivot_calc <- ACC_mult_sex_pos_pivot_damage %>%
  transform(`F` = as.numeric(Female)/as.numeric(ACC_mult_sex_pos_pivot_damage[nrow(ACC_mult_sex_pos_pivot_damage), "Female"])) %>%
  transform(`M` = as.numeric(Male)/as.numeric(ACC_mult_sex_pos_pivot_damage[nrow(ACC_mult_sex_pos_pivot_damage), "Male"])) %>%
  dplyr::select(c(Mutation,
                  `F`,
                  `M`)) %>%
  subset(Mutation %in% unique(as.vector(multcancerpivotpos_melted_over0.01$Mutation)))

ACC_sole_sex_pos_pivot_calc <- ACC_sole_sex_pos_pivot_damage %>%
  transform(`F` = as.numeric(Female)/as.numeric(ACC_sole_sex_pos_pivot_damage[nrow(ACC_sole_sex_pos_pivot_damage), "Female"])) %>%
  transform(`M` = as.numeric(Male)/as.numeric(ACC_sole_sex_pos_pivot_damage[nrow(ACC_sole_sex_pos_pivot_damage), "Male"])) %>%
  dplyr::select(c(Mutation,

                  `M`)) %>%

ACC_mult_agestrata_pos_pivot_calc <- ACC_mult_agestrata_pos_pivot_damage %>%
  transform(`0 - 9` = as.numeric(ACC_mult_agestrata_pos_pivot_damage[,2])/as.numeric(ACC_mult_agestrata_pos_pivot_damage[nrow(ACC_mult_agestrata_pos_pivot_damage), 
                                                                                                                         colnames(ACC_mult_agestrata_pos_pivot_damage)[2]])) %>%

# melt pos pivot tables and add number of individuals to sex or age strata listed, already do >= 1% proportion 
ACC_mult_sex_pos_pivot_melted <- reshape2::melt(ACC_mult_sex_pos_pivot_calc) %>%
  dplyr::rename(Sex = variable,
                Proportion = value) %>%
  arrange(-Proportion) %>%
  transform(Sex = ifelse(Sex == "F",
                         paste0("Female (",
                                as.numeric(ACC_mult_sex_pos_pivot_damage[nrow(ACC_mult_sex_pos_pivot_damage), "Female"]),
                                " individuals)"),
                         as.character(Sex))) %>%
  transform(Sex = ifelse(Sex == "M",
                         paste0("Male (",
                                as.numeric(ACC_mult_sex_pos_pivot_damage[nrow(ACC_mult_sex_pos_pivot_damage), "Male"]),
                                " individuals)"),
                         Sex)) %>%
  transform(Sex = ifelse(grepl("\\(1 ", 
                               Sex),
                         gsub("individuals", 
                              "individual",
                              Sex),
                         Sex)) %>%
  subset(Mutation %in% (reshape2::melt(ACC_mult_sex_pos_pivot_calc) %>%
                          dplyr::rename(Sex = variable,
                                        Proportion = value) %>%
                          arrange(-Proportion) %>%
                          subset(Proportion >= 0.01) %>%
                          pull(Mutation) %>%
                          unique() %>%
                          as.vector())) %>%
  remove_rownames()
```
